schema_note: Additive, bounded evidence-fidelity correction to feature-engine-mutation-material-gap-identity-resolution-002.json, remediating ChatGPT Review A's REVISION_REQUIRED verdict (0 Blocker / 1 Major / 0 Minor, Risk R1) -- P3-FEATURE-EVID03-COND2-RES002-A-MAJ-01. resolution-002.json is NOT modified -- it remains immutable, byte-unchanged, preserved as historical evidence.

finding_remediated.defect: resolution-002.json classified 72 rows SUCCESSOR_MATCH — CURRENT KILLED but did not durably identify, per historical row, the exact current successor mutant ID, exact current mutation diff, or exact Evidence-005 status. All 128 rows recorded current_evidence_005_status as effectively N/A. Function-level aggregate kill/survive counts (e.g. prepare_swing_confirmed: 46 killed / 7 survived) cannot establish that the SPECIFIC mutant representing a historical semantic obligation is the killed one.

remediation_method: For each of the 72 originally-claimed SUCCESSOR_MATCH rows, independently reconstructed the exact current mutant diff by extracting the disposable mutation workspace's own trampoline source (mutants/src/feature_engine/<module>.py -- mutmut 3.x stores ALL mutant variants of a function as separate __mutmut_N function definitions in ONE file, plus a true __mutmut_orig baseline) and diffing each candidate against __mutmut_orig via Python difflib -- content-identical to `tooling show` output, without requiring any mutation test execution. Cross-referenced the historical row's exact field/argument/operator/literal description against the exact current diff content (not function-level aggregates, not naming, not operator category alone) to identify the UNIQUE current mutant ID representing that specific historical obligation. Looked up that exact current mutant ID's status directly in Evidence-005's full_current_mutant_mapping -- Evidence-005 itself was not rerun, not altered.
important_result_note: Evidence fidelity was prioritized over preserving the prior 72-row count. Rigorous per-row diff verification found: 70 of the original 72 rows DO uniquely and exactly identify a current killed mutant (the underlying technical claim holds, now with durable exact evidence). 2 of the original 72 rows, on close inspection, could NOT be uniquely resolved to one current mutant (a sibling historical row shared the identical generic description and both plausibly map to either of two distinct current mutation sites) -- these 2 are honestly reclassified AMBIGUOUS — MULTIPLE POSSIBLE SUCCESSORS rather than forced onto an arbitrary candidate. No row's underlying successor-function identification (the 53 BEHAVIOR_REMOVED rows, the original 3 AMBIGUOUS rows) required re-review and none is touched by this correction.
